goal:
Optimize the XSBench macroscopic cross-section lookup kernel in src/ for speed — higher lookups_per_sec (single-threaded, event-based, H-M small, unionized grid; see scripts/config.sh) — while keeping results bit-identical: the verification checksum printed by the binary must equal the frozen reference in benchmarks/reference_hash.txt. The evaluation scripts (scripts/) and the frozen reference numbers (benchmarks/) are fixed by the harness.

Calibration, measured on comparable single-core hardware: the unmodified kernel runs at ~1.45M lookups_per_sec; optimizations that keep the existing lookup structure land near 2.5M; substantially restructured kernels have exceeded 3.2M. The plausibility cap is 8M.
gate_block:
Only modify files under src/. The harness runs, in order:
  - bash scripts/check_verify.sh   (VERIFY gate: bit-identical checksums at several lookup lengths)
  - bash scripts/bench.sh          (objective: lookups_per_sec; also emits the RATE_PLAUSIBLE gate token)
A change is accepted only if VERIFY=PASS and RATE_PLAUSIBLE=PASS; among accepted changes, higher lookups_per_sec is better. scripts/config.sh fixes the benchmark run (-m event -s small -G unionized -t 1 -l 2000000). RATE_PLAUSIBLE caps lookups_per_sec at 8M to reject timing cheats (moving the lookup work into untimed init and streaming precomputed results in the timed loop) that would otherwise keep VERIFY bit-identical. Both scripts can be run mid-research to measure progress; the harness re-measures from a pristine checkout of your final src/ at the exit.
